subject: Decimal places and standardised correlation coefficients/estimates

messages.author: 570debbdb91283e7
messages.subject: Decimal places and standardised correlation coefficients/estimates
parts:
Hi group

When I calculate the standardised correlation coefficient between two variables, the figure is 3.2.  When I calculate the standardised parameter estimates in lavaan, the figure is .32.  Why is there this discrepancy?  I'm pretty sure I'm missing something very simple here.

Many thanks
Reflex

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Decimal places and standardised correlation coefficients/estimates
parts: When I calculate the standardised correlation coefficient between two variables, the figure is 3.2.

A Pearson correlation coefficient is standardized by definition (the SDs of each variable are in the denominator).  It can't exceed 1, so your calculation must be incorrect if the result is 3.2

I'm not sure how much this has to do with lavaan, but posting your syntax (and data if possible) is more more likely to result in helpful feedback than a vague description.

Terry

messages.author: 570debbdb91283e7
messages.subject: Re: Decimal places and standardised correlation coefficients/estimates
parts:
Hi Terrence thanks very much for your reply.

As you can tell, I am an R beginner.  I realised it was because in the output the 3.2 figure had e-01 after it to designate that the figure was actually .32.  I found that the following command turns scientific notation off: options(scipen=999).

Many thanks
reflex
